newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania wheat may run out by end-May, official says.
newsitem.headline: Romania wheat may run out by end-May, official says.

text.p: A shortage of wheat following last year's poor crop may force Romania to import to meet demand for bread and bakery products in the first half of 1997, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"Our wheat reserves might run out by the end of May," the offical said.
The official said the ministry had decided to use some 550,000 tonnes of wheat from the country's strategic reserves to ensure flour supplies to state-run and private bakeries.
"So I'm afraid that we will have to import certain quantities, to be on the safe side," the official said, adding that he could not elaborate on the level of expected imports.
The wheat harvest in Romania is completed by mid-July.

Romania had 2.11 million of hectares under wheat last year. But an early and prolonged winter damaged the crop on half that area, giving the country less than 60 percent of its bumper crop of some 7.8 million tonnes in 1995, when exports amounted to 1.3 million tonnes.
The poor 1996 crop, enough only to meet part of domestic consumption and replenish state reserves, ruined the cash-strapped country's plans to export grain.
Ministry data show wheat was sown on 2.1 million hectares last autumn, and that the country expects a wheat crop of around 6.0 million tonnes this year.
